Author: namibj
Content:
If we're lucky I can draw up a suitable voltage supply (probably also acting as more-accurate-than-current ADC reference) add-on board for the bond tester's expansion header within about 100 hours from now; I'd then suggest we'd pack two of the 5 (if ordered min cheap quantity) along with a confirmed working bond tester and the suggested 2 bond-check-passed COBs of each of the 3 FlexMem dies together into a parcel and ship to Germany; I'm _assuming_ the bond tester I'm offered is in China currently? Feel free to ask where it is/if it's there; I'd then try to get the programmable voltage supply for the low voltage testing that thus checks data resilience at "power save" sleep-supply-voltages (and indirectly confirms the array itself to be robust even if not directly qualifying a particular access speed) prepped at JLCPCB to conveniently get where the other bond testers are.

Then the idea would be that I'd try to program it later next week/weekend-after-next, and once it's working for me someone who can be trusted enough to not break the gear or steal the parts could use one of the other bond testers with the add-on board and test a statistically significant quantity of those 150 FlexMem dies.

To be clear, I'm not against doing that myself, but I don't currently have the resources to do much fancy beyond maybe putting a few DUTs with the board into a filament dryer offering concern at up to about 65C.

Author: namibj
Content:
If you'd want to help, a non-expensive 1% (ish) LDO that can do like 50 mA at outputs programmable from two digital RPiPico2 pins and voltages from at least like 3~3.4 ish Volts down to at LEAST 500 mV, ideally I'd want it down to about 300 mV. 
Ideally one that's stocked at JLCPCB, but worst case their ability to order from mouser/digikey at a unit price premium and handle the logistics for you would give that as an escape but I'd prefer not to, due to it being prone to delays.

[Mostly I'm not sure if the SRAM control can behave itself enough at the very low voltage end; I'd probably expect most cells to retain even at very very low supply.]

Author: namibj
Content:
I've figured out a way to do programmable LDO with commodity parts: a 12 bit I2C DAC and an "adjustable"-style LDO, and a 3-resistor weighted summer mixing Vout/GND/Vdac at the LDO's FB node.
Should easily give about 1mV steps from around 50 mV to around 3.2-ish V.

Well, technically Gemini did the looking for me but I'm pretty sure those parts are actually commodity (or very similar ones at least).

I wasn't planning on deleting the pull-up but rather adding a preload to GND to overpower R12 and give the LDO some nicer operating conditions.

I'll try to get a layout on Wednesday; if there's no plan yet regarding what kind of header that is, may I request that to be decreed by then to allow including a matching connector and board orientation to go with it?

Any preference about I2C assignment to the two GPIOs on the header? I'd put one of them simple EEPROMs on it I guess...

Should I provide precise 3.3V on it as well or would that be counter-productive due to how invasive the changes to the tester board would be for custom 3v3 supply? I could probably go for just calibrating the ADC by muxing COMA and COME together, I'd hope the existing 3v3 reference doesn't drift wildly within a minute or so at least...
